module.purpose: Provides the server-side request orchestration entry point for rendering a TanStack Router request into a Response, including router setup, loading, SSR dehydration, callback execution, response binding, abort handling, and cleanup.
module.summary: This module builds per-request router state from an incoming Request, normalizes its URL, creates in-memory navigation history, loads route data, handles redirects, waits for SSR dehydration, and delegates response generation to a callback. It coordinates abort-aware promises through a WeakMap of request waiters and ensures SSR resources are cleaned up unless a streaming response owns cleanup.
module.businessContext: Supports server-side rendering for routed web requests. Failures can produce incomplete HTML, incorrect redirects, leaked SSR state, or responses that ignore client cancellation.
functions: removeRequestWaiter (~L23-38): Removes a settled rejection waiter while preserving active registrations.
waitForRequest (~L40-88): Makes promise completion respect request abortion and late-result cleanup.
createRequestHandler (~L90-173): Orchestrates router initialization, SSR loading, response generation, and cleanup.
getRequestHeaders (~L175-185): Collects rendered-match headers and merges them with HTML defaults.

mutationOfArg: Registers an abort listener on the request signal.
Mutates waiter arrays and the request waiter WeakMap.
Mutates the per-request router through SSR attachment, history update, loading, and cleanup.

sectionMap.name: abort-fast-path
sectionMap.intent: Rejects immediately when the request signal has already aborted.
branchOutcomes: aborted: attach late-result handler and reject

sectionMap.name: waiter-registration
sectionMap.intent: Registers promise rejection callbacks and installs one abort listener per signal.
branchOutcomes: new signal: create waiter list and abort listener

sectionMap.name: promise-settlement
sectionMap.intent: Resolves active requests, reports late values, and propagates promise errors.

sectionMap.name: router-ssr-orchestration
sectionMap.intent: Initializes router SSR state, history, route loading, dehydration, and headers.

sectionMap.name: redirect-handling
sectionMap.intent: Returns server-generated redirects without invoking the response callback.
branchOutcomes: non-redirect result: continue SSR response generation

sectionMap.name: response-binding
sectionMap.intent: Invokes the callback and binds its response to request-scoped SSR lifecycle.

sectionMap.name: cleanup-selection
sectionMap.intent: Cleans up SSR state unless a streaming response owns cleanup.
branchOutcomes: cleanup owned externally: skip router cleanup
cleanup not owned externally: invoke router cleanup

sectionMap.name: rendered-header-collection
sectionMap.intent: Collects headers from rendered matches before merging response defaults.

units.name: removeRequestWaiter

detail.name: removeRequestWaiter
detail.signature: function removeRequestWaiter(waiters: Array<RequestWaiter>, index: number, reject: (reason: unknown) => void)
preconditions: waiters is an array of request waiter entries.
index identifies the candidate entry in waiters.
reject is the rejection callback whose identity is being removed.
postconditions: If waiters[index] is not the same function object as reject, waiters is unchanged.
If a matching entry is not the final array element, its slot is set to undefined and the array length is unchanged.
If a matching entry is the final array element, it is removed and the array length decreases by one.
invariants: Removal is based on strict identity comparison between waiters[index] and reject.
No other waiter entry is intentionally changed.
edgeCases: A stale or mismatched reject callback at the requested index causes a no-op.
A matching non-final entry is cleared without shifting subsequent entries.
A matching final entry is removed from the end of the array.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: A non-matching or out-of-range index results in no mutation.

stateMutations: Mutates the waiters array by clearing a matching non-final slot or removing a matching final entry.
detail.summary: Removes a specific request waiter from the supplied waiter list only when the entry at the given index is the same rejection callback. Non-terminal entries are cleared in place, while a matching terminal entry is removed from the list.

specTests.then: the matching slot is set to undefined, later entries remain in their original positions, and the array length is unchanged
the final entry is removed and the array length decreases by one

units.name: waitForRequest

detail.name: waitForRequest
detail.signature: export function waitForRequest<T>(value: T | PromiseLike<T>, signal: AbortSignal, onLate?: (value: T) => void): Promise<T>
preconditions: The value must be either a value of type T or a thenable compatible with PromiseLike<T>.
The signal must be an AbortSignal.
postconditions: If the signal does not abort first, the returned promise fulfills with the resolved value or rejects with the input promise's rejection reason.
If the signal aborts before settlement, the returned promise rejects with signal.reason.
If the value fulfills after the signal has aborted, onLate is invoked with that value when provided.
The request's abort waiter is removed after the input promise settles.
invariants: At most one waiter is registered for this invocation.
An abort signal is associated with a shared waiter collection and its abort listener is registered once for that collection.
An already-aborted signal causes immediate rejection without registering a new waiter.
edgeCases: When signal.aborted is already true, the returned promise rejects with signal.reason and a subsequently fulfilled value is passed to onLate if provided.
When the input value is an already fulfilled non-promise value, the returned promise fulfills asynchronously with that value unless the signal aborts first.
When the input promise rejects, the returned promise rejects with the same rejection reason.
When the signal aborts while waiting, all waiters associated with that signal reject with signal.reason and the waiter collection is cleared.
When a value fulfills after abortion, it is not used to fulfill the returned promise; it is only sent to onLate when that callback is provided.

errorPolicy.returnsOnError: Returns a rejected Promise: signal.reason when aborted before settlement, otherwise the input promise's rejection reason.

stateMutations: Adds or removes this invocation's reject callback in the requestWaiters collection keyed by signal.
Creates and deletes the signal's requestWaiters entry as needed.
Registers a one-time abort event listener on a signal for a newly created waiter collection.
Clears the waiter collection when the signal aborts.
detail.summary: Waits for a value or promise to settle unless the supplied abort signal fires first. Aborted requests reject with the signal reason, while a value that fulfills afterward is delivered to the optional late-result callback.

specTests.then: The returned promise rejects with abortReason, and onLate is invoked with 42 after the value settles.

specTests.when: The signal aborts before the promise fulfills, then the promise fulfills with 42
specTests.then: The returned promise rejects with the signal reason and onLate is invoked with 42.

units.name: createRequestHandler

detail.name: createRequestHandler
detail.signature: export function createRequestHandler<TRouter extends AnyRouter>({ createRouter, request, getRouterManifest, }: { createRouter: () => TRouter; request: Request; getRouterManifest?: () => ServerManifest | Promise<ServerManifest>; }): RequestHandler<TRouter>

parameters.name: { createRouter, request, getRouterManifest }
parameters.type: { createRouter: () => TRouter; request: Request; getRouterManifest?: () => ServerManifest | Promise<ServerManifest>; }

preconditions: createRouter must produce a compatible router instance.
request must be a Request whose URL and AbortSignal can be used for SSR processing.
The callback supplied to the returned RequestHandler must produce a compatible SSR response value.
postconditions: On normal non-redirect completion, returns the response produced by binding the callback result to the request and router SSR state.
If the router produces a redirect result, returns that redirect response without invoking the callback.
Router SSR cleanup is performed unless the resulting response owns cleanup through streaming.
invariants: The request AbortSignal is checked before router creation and at each major SSR stage.
The router is updated with a memory history initialized from the normalized request URL.
The router origin is preserved when configured; otherwise it is derived from the request.
A detached or late callback result is disposed when request processing is aborted or otherwise detached.
edgeCases: If the request is already aborted before handler execution, processing stops immediately and the router factory is not invoked.
If getRouterManifest is absent, SSR initialization proceeds without a manifest value.
If getRouterManifest returns either a manifest or a promise, initialization waits for its resolved value.
If router loading yields a redirect result, that redirect is returned and the response callback is skipped.
If an error or abort occurs before a streaming response takes ownership of cleanup, router SSR cleanup still runs.
If the callback result is detached or arrives after request cancellation, it is disposed using the request signal reason.

raises: Abort errors or the request signal's abort reason when the request is aborted.
Errors propagated from manifest resolution, router initialization, router loading, dehydration, response-header generation, callback execution, response binding, or SSR cleanup.
errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: No custom invalid-input conversion is performed; errors from the supplied dependencies or request processing are propagated.

stateMutations: Creates and updates the supplied router with SSR utilities, memory history, and origin.
Triggers router loading and SSR dehydration.
May mutate router.serverSsr state through response binding and cleanup.
detail.ioFormatSpec: Consumes a Fetch Request and returns a RequestHandler<TRouter>. The handler supplies the callback with { request, router, responseHeaders } and returns the bound SSR Response, or a router redirect response.
detail.summary: Creates a request-scoped SSR request handler for the supplied router factory and Request. The returned handler initializes router SSR state, loads the request, handles redirects, invokes the response callback, and ensures SSR cleanup according to response ownership.

specLiterals.role: Fallback base origin used while normalizing the request URL.
Router server-result type indicating that the redirect response must be returned directly.
SSR cleanup ownership value indicating that the response stream performs cleanup.

specTests.then: It rejects with the signal's abort error or reason and does not create or load a router.

specTests.when: The returned request handler is invoked.
specTests.then: It returns that redirect response and does not invoke the response callback.

detail.name: getRequestHeaders
preconditions: opts.router is an AnyRouter with an accessible matches store.
postconditions: Returns a Headers instance containing the merged headers from the router's rendered matches.
invariants: Each rendered match's headers is included in the merge input in rendered-match iteration order.
edgeCases: When the router has no rendered matches, the merge operation receives an empty header collection.
detail.summary: Builds a Headers object by collecting headers from the router's rendered matches and merging them.
